question: Honeywell reported Q2 2026 a few weeks after spinning off Aerospace. What were consolidated sales vs sales excluding Aerospace, and why is GAAP EPS from continuing operations so far above adjusted EPS?
grading: Use HON, CIK 773840. Consolidated sales USD 9,719M; ex-Aerospace sales USD 5,187M. Identify the Quantinuum gain removal (-$15.87/share) as the main EPS adjustment. State actual Q2 close June 27, spin June 29 in Q3, and Aerospace consolidated in Q2 with discontinued-operations presentation beginning Q3. Keep consolidated and ex-Aerospace EPS bases distinct.
answer: HON consolidated Q2 2026 sales were USD 9,719 million; sales excluding Aerospace were USD 5,187 million. Consolidated GAAP continuing-operations EPS of $17.83 reconciles to adjusted EPS of $4.52, principally by removing $15.87 per share of Quantinuum deconsolidation gains; other net adjustments add $2.56. Ex-Aerospace EPS was $16.65 GAAP / $1.95 adjusted. The Q2 actual close was June 27, although presented as June 30: the June 29 Aerospace spin occurred in Q3. Aerospace remains consolidated in this Q2 presentation and becomes discontinued operations beginning Q3. [G25-E1, G25-E2]

output.answer:
## Headline numbers (Q2 2026, reported July 23, 2026)

| Metric | Consolidated Honeywell (incl. Aerospace) | Honeywell Technologies (excl. Aerospace) | 2Q25 (HT basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | $9,719M, +4% reported/organic | $5,187M, +3% reported / +4% organic | $5,018M |
| GAAP EPS (continuing ops) | $17.83 (+312%) | $16.65 | $1.21 |
| Adjusted EPS | $4.52 (−4%) | $1.95 (+10%) | $1.77 |

Aerospace itself (now Honeywell Aerospace, NASDAQ: HONA) reported $4.52B of sales, +5%, as a standalone for the quarter — that's the "separation adjustment" bridging $9.7B consolidated to $5.2B.

## Why GAAP EPS is so far above adjusted EPS

Almost entirely one non-cash, one-time item: a **$6,629 million pretax gain on the deconsolidation of Quantinuum**, which IPO'd on June 4, 2026 and ceased to be consolidated (Honeywell retained a ~47% stake). In the per-share reconciliation this appears as a **(15.87)** adjustment — i.e., GAAP EPS of $16.65 for Honeywell Technologies (and $17.83 consolidated) includes roughly $15.87/share of paper gain that adjusted EPS strips out.

The bridge runs the other way from there: GAAP is *reduced (added back)* by items like the ~$0.65/share equity loss on the retained Quantinuum stake, divestiture-related costs (~$820M in the quarter), impairment of assets held for sale, acquisition-related intangible amortization (~$0.32), ERP costs, and Russia-Ukraine impacts. Adjusted EPS excludes all of these by definition — the company defines it as diluted GAAP EPS from continuing operations less those specified charges (and, for the Technologies basis, also removes pension income and Quantinuum results across all periods).

So the gap is not operating performance: the operating story is the opposite direction — segment margin expanded 30 bps consolidated (23.1%) and 90 bps to 19.0% for Honeywell Technologies, with Building Automation up 10% to $2.0B. Consolidated adjusted EPS actually *fell* 4% (partly a higher tax rate), while Technologies adjusted EPS rose 10%. Note also that adjusted EPS across periods now reflects a 1-for-2 reverse stock split, which makes the raw GAAP-vs-adjusted per-share gap look especially large.

Sources:
- Honeywell Technologies Q2 2026 earnings release: https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/news/press-releases/2026/07/honeywell-technologies-reports-second-quarter-results
- SEC Exhibit 99 (full reconciliation tables): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/773840/000077384026000120/exhibit99-q22026earningsre.htm
- Q2 2026 earnings presentation (EPS bridge): https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/560c97b2-6ca1-4c77-a281-06ea18af20b7
- July 8, 2026 guidance update re: reverse split: https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/news/press-releases/2026/07/honeywell-technologies-updates-2026-financial-guidance-following-reverse-stock-split
- Honeywell Aerospace standalone Q2: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/honeywell-aerospace-reports-second-quarter-200500878.html
